description.narrative: Founded in 1978, Parliamentarians for Global Action (PGA) is an international non-governmental network of individual MPs with a cross-party background. The PGA has about 1000 members from 150 countries in all parts of the world. The PGA mobilizes parliamentarians who advocate for human rights and the rule of law, democracy, human security, inclusion, gender equality and justice, including climate justice and the environment. This is done through training, awareness-raising, building technical capacity and strengthening the capacity of parliamentarians to take ownership, initiative and legislative action. This effort aims to strengthen the rights of LGBTQI+ people at the national level. The programme works to strengthen democratic resilience and counteract the global democratic backlash and the emergence of anti-rights movements. This one-year programme focuses on parliamentarians, i.e. policymakers, and thus well positioned to translate international human rights commitments into concrete parliamentary action at the national level. The aim of the programme is concrete results at the national level to improve the lives of LGBTQI+ people and human rights defenders. The programme will 1) organise strategic parliamentary gatherings to share good practices and build a regional and international network; 2) develop methods to provide sustainability beyond the one-year programming period; and 3) arrange dialogue between parliamentarians and civil society. Its overarching objective is: Strengthen democratic governance, human rights and freedoms by building the political will and capacity of parliamentarians to promote rights-based, inclusive and responsible legislative processes, with a focus on equality in sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC).

Parliamentarians for Global Action (PGA) grundades 1978 och är ett icke-statligt internationellt nätverk av enskilda parlamentsledamöter med partiöverskridande bakgrund. PGA har omkring 1000 medlemmar från 150 länder i alla delar av världen. PGA mobiliserar parlamentariker som förespråkar mänskliga rättigheter och rättsstatens principer, demokrati, mänsklig säkerhet, inkludering, jämställdhet och rättvisa, inklusive klimaträttvisa och miljö. Detta sker genom utbildning, medvetenhet, uppbyggnad av teknisk kapacitet och stärkande av parlamentarikernas kapacitet att ta ägarskap, initiativ och lagstiftningsåtgärder. Denna insats syftar till att stärka HBTQI+-personers rättigheter på nationell nivå. Programmet verkar för att stärka den demokratiska motståndskraften och motverka den globala demokratiska tillbakagången och framväxten av anti-rättighetsrörelser. Detta ettåriga program fokuserar på parlamentarikerna, dvs politiska beslutsfattare, och därmed väl positionerade att omvandla internationella mänskliga rättighetsåtaganden till konkreta parlamentariska åtgärder på nationell nivå. Målet med programmet är konkreta resultat på nationell nivå för att förbättra livet för HBTQI+-personer och människorättsförsvarare. Programmet kommer 1) att arrangera strategiska parlamentariska sammankomster för att dela goda metoder och bygga ett regionalt och internationellt nätverk; 2) utveckla metoder för att ge hållbarhet utöver den ettåriga programperioden; och 3) arrangera dialog mellan parlamentariker och civilsamhälle. Dess övergripande mål är: Stärka demokratisk styrning, mänskliga rättigheter och friheter genom att bygga parlamentarikernas politiska vilja och kapacitet att främja rättighetsbaserade, inkluderande och ansvarsfulla lagstiftningsprocesser, med fokus på jämlikhet vad gäller sexuell läggning, könsidentitet och uttryck samt könskaraktäristika (SOGIESC).

Overall Objective: Strengthen democratic governance, human rights, and freedoms by building the political will and capacity of parliamentarians to promote rights-based, inclusive, and accountable legislative processes, with a focus on equality related to sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC).
Outcome 1: Strengthened parliamentary capacity and engagement for inclusive governance and rights protection
Parliamentarians demonstrate increased knowledge, confidence, and willingness to promote inclusive, rights-based legislative and oversight processes, including protection of fundamental freedoms such as expression, association, and participation. This is reinforced through strengthened cross-regional peer exchange, sustained parliamentary networks, and structured opportunities for collaboration and mutual learning.
Outcome 2: Enhanced collaboration between parliamentarians and civil society
Structured engagement between parliamentarians and civil society actors - particularly LGBTQI organizations and human rights defenders - is strengthened, contributing to more informed and inclusive legislative processes, thereby contributing to more open civic space and safer conditions for civil society engagement.
Outcome 3: Increased use of practical legislative tools for inclusion
Parliamentarians access and utilize context-specific tools to support inclusive legislative drafting, oversight, and policy engagement, including the protection of fundamental freedoms, accountability, and rule of law.
PGA's vision is to strengthen a rules-based international order for an equitable, safe, sustainable, and democratic world.
As a non-governmental, multi-party, international network of legislators acting in their individual capacity, PGA informs and mobilizes parliamentarians in all regions of the world to advocate for human rights and the rule of law, democracy, human security, inclusion, gender equality and justice, including climate justice, and the environment.
